title: Bài sưu tầm 137 - Passage 1: The Cochineal Insect: From Aztec Crimson to Modern Industry
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 1 — TEST 137

The Cochineal Insect: From Aztec Crimson to Modern Industry

Paragraph 1. For over three centuries, the richest red textiles worn by European monarchs and generals owed their brilliance not to a mineral or a plant, but to a tiny parasitic insect from Mexico. Known as cochineal (Dactylopius coccus), the creature spends almost its entire life motionless, feeding on the moisture inside flat cactus pads while shielding itself beneath a white waxy coating. To defend against predators, the wingless females accumulate high concentrations of carminic acid, a compound that produces an intense crimson pigment when crushed.

Paragraph 2. Long before Europeans reached the Americas, Indigenous farmers in southern Mexico domesticated the insect in carefully tended plantations. Under Aztec rule, conquered towns were required to send sacks of dried cochineal to the imperial capital each year as regular tax payments, where the dye coloured ceremonial cloaks, murals, and codices. Harvesting was delicate work: workers gently swept the mature insects off the thorny pads using soft brushes made from deer tails before drying them in the sun or over low ovens.

Paragraph 3. When Spanish ships carried the first dried batches back to Seville in the 1520s, European dyers quickly recognized that cochineal yielded shades far brighter and longer-lasting than local roots or kermes insects. By the seventeenth century, cochineal ranked behind only silver as the most valuable export shipped out of New Spain. To protect this lucrative monopoly, Spanish authorities kept the biological origin of the dye a strict secret, banning foreigners from visiting Mexican production districts on pain of death. As a result, many European merchants remained convinced for decades that the dried purple grains were actually tiny plant seeds.

Paragraph 4. In 1777, a French botanist named Nicolas-Joseph Thiéry de Menonville risked imprisonment by travelling in disguise to Oaxaca, where he smuggled living cochineal-covered plants aboard a ship bound for the Caribbean. Although his French colonial plantation ultimately failed, Spanish control weakened after Mexico gained independence in 1821. Soon the Canary Islands became a major producer, helped by an arid climate ideal for host cacti. Britain's textile mills bought enormous quantities to dye military uniforms and heavy wool garments destined for export.

Paragraph 5. The boom ended abruptly in the mid-nineteenth century with the arrival of artificial aniline dyes synthesized from coal tar. Because factory-made reds cost a fraction of imported insect pigment and required no agricultural labour, global demand for cochineal collapsed within twenty years. Only small rural communities in Peru and the Canary Islands kept traditional cultivation alive for local weavers and artists.

Paragraph 6. Remarkably, cochineal experienced an unexpected revival in the late twentieth century. As health regulators restricted several synthetic red colourings after linking them to allergic reactions in consumers, manufacturers turned back to natural carmine. Today, Peru supplies over eighty percent of the global harvest, which is used widely in fruit yoghurts, juices, and luxury cosmetics such as lipsticks. Because the pigment is derived from insects rather than plants, food companies in many countries are now required to label it explicitly on packaging.

groups.title: Questions 8–13
groups.instructions:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 8–13 on your answer sheet, write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "...feeding on the moisture inside flat cactus pads..."
Từ cần điền: cactus.
Đoạn 2: "...swept the mature insects off the thorny pads using soft brushes..."
Từ cần điền: brushes.
Đoạn 3: "...Spanish authorities kept the biological origin of the dye a strict secret..."
Từ cần điền: secret.
Đoạn 3: "...many European merchants remained convinced for decades that the dried purple grains were actually tiny plant seeds."
Từ cần điền: seeds.
Đoạn 4: "...Britain's textile mills bought enormous quantities to dye military uniforms and heavy wool garments..."
Từ cần điền: wool.
Đoạn 5: "...artificial aniline dyes synthesized from coal tar."
Từ cần điền: coal.
Đoạn 6: "...used widely in fruit yoghurts, juices, and luxury cosmetics such as lipsticks."
Từ cần điền: cosmetics.

q8.text: The Aztecs were the first civilization to learn how to breed cochineal insects in Mexico.

steps: Đoạn 2: Bài nói nông dân bản địa đã thuần hóa loài này từ trước đó, còn đế chế Aztec thu cống nạp từ các thị trấn bị chinh phục (conquered towns were required to send... to the imperial capital) chứ không phải Aztec là nền văn minh đầu tiên nuôi.
Kết luận: Chọn FALSE.

q9.text: Only one other commodity shipped from Spanish Mexico generated more export revenue than cochineal during the 1600s.

steps: Đoạn 3: Vào thế kỷ 17, cochineal chỉ đứng sau mỗi bạc (ranked behind only silver as the most valuable export).
Kết luận: Chọn TRUE.

q10.text: Thiéry de Menonville received financial backing from the French king for his expedition to Oaxaca.

steps: Đoạn 4: Có nhắc nhà thực vật học Pháp lén sang Oaxaca lấy giống mang về thuộc địa Pháp, nhưng hoàn toàn không nhắc chuyến đi có được nhà vua Pháp tài trợ tiền hay không.
Kết luận: Chọn NOT GIVEN.

q11.text: The lower cost of synthetic alternatives led to a rapid decline in cochineal farming.

steps: Đoạn 5: Thuốc nhuộm nhân tạo rẻ hơn rất nhiều khiến nhu cầu cochineal sụp đổ chỉ trong vòng 20 năm.
Kết luận: Chọn TRUE.

q12.text: Cochineal returned to commercial popularity mainly because it produces brighter shades than artificial food dyes.

steps: Đoạn 6: Nguyên nhân hồi sinh là do cơ quan y tế siết các phẩm màu tổng hợp gây dị ứng (restricted several synthetic red colourings after linking them to allergic reactions), không phải do màu tươi hơn.
Kết luận: Chọn FALSE.

q13.text: Consumer groups in Peru campaigned for strict rules on how cochineal is listed on food labels.

steps: Đoạn 6: Có nhắc Peru sản xuất phần lớn và nhắc nhiều nước yêu cầu ghi nhãn rõ, nhưng không đề cập có nhóm người tiêu dùng ở Peru vận động cho quy định ghi nhãn này hay không.
Kết luận: Chọn NOT GIVEN.
